projects.title: To-do List Application
projects.summary: A C++17 desktop application built with Qt Widgets and CMake. Its source implements adding, completing and deleting tasks, with local JSON storage between sessions.

caseStudy.overview: A small desktop task manager with a text input, checkable task list, Add button and Delete Selected button.
caseStudy.question: Practice combining C++ with a minimal desktop interface and immediate visual feedback when tasks are completed, as described in the project README.
approach: Build a desktop interface with Qt Widgets and C++17, using CMake.
Add tasks with the Add button or Enter, ignoring blank entries.
Store tasks in tasks.json in the app's data directory and load them when the app starts.

demonstration.description: The screenshot above is the original image published in the project README. It shows a checked task and the application controls. This portfolio review verified the source; it did not run the desktop app.

results: The source implements marking tasks complete with a strikethrough style and deleting selected tasks.
It saves the task list locally after changes and when the window is closed.
limitations: These capabilities were checked in the public source; the application has not been run during this portfolio review.
Completion status, release packaging and cross-platform behavior have not been verified.
nextSteps: Run the desktop app and document its setup, save/load behavior and known issues.
Confirm its completion status and release packaging.

projects.title: CSV business report
projects.summary: A Python/pandas script for cleaning business CSV data and producing sales reports. The included synthetic dataset demonstrates its calculations; the tool remains in progress.

caseStudy.overview: A command-line script that reads sales records, cleans selected fields and writes a cleaned CSV plus a sales summary. It is intended as a reusable business-data cleaning tool and remains in progress.
caseStudy.question: Create a reusable script that cleans business data and generates a readable sales report. The included generated sales records demonstrate its current behavior.
approach: Use pandas to normalize column and product text and remove exact duplicate rows.
Convert dates, quantities and prices; stop for missing or unparseable dates, quantities or prices, nonpositive quantities or negative prices.
Calculate quantity × unit price for each row, aggregate revenue and units, and group revenue by product.
Write cleaned_sales.csv and a UTF-8 text report using pathlib.

codeExample.caption: Revenue calculations from main.py, lines 57–60; inline comments omitted.
codeExample.content:
df["total_sales"] = df["quantity"] * df["unit_price"]
total_revenue = df["total_sales"].sum()
total_units = df["quantity"].sum()
sales_by_product = df.groupby("product")["total_sales"].sum()

demonstration.description: The text below is the saved report from the included generated sales records. An isolated run reproduced it exactly; the totals were also checked independently against the input.

output.caption: Actual saved report · generated sales dataset · currency symbol as supplied in the project
output.content:
SALES REPORT
============

Total revenue: $4,005.00
Total units sold: 24
Duplicate rows removed: 0

Revenue by product:
Product             Revenue
---------------------------
Keyboard        $225.00
Laptop          $3,000.00
Monitor         $540.00
Mouse           $240.00

results: An isolated run reproduced the saved report from the 10-row included input file: $4,005.00 total revenue, 24 units and zero duplicate rows removed.
Revenue by product in that file is Laptop $3,000.00, Monitor $540.00, Mouse $240.00 and Keyboard $225.00. These are dataset calculations, not claims of real-business impact.
limitations: The sales dataset is generated for demonstration. Its totals do not describe a real company or establish business impact.
Required-column validation occurs after columns are accessed. An isolated missing-unit_price check raised a KeyError before the intended friendly error message.
No README, dependency manifest, automated project tests or public repository was found for this project.
nextSteps: Document setup and the generated dataset, then expand validation before using the script with other business CSV files.
Move the required-column check before column access, then add validation tests and reproducible setup instructions. These improvements have not yet been implemented.
